description: Spatial statistics test: do Chinese-linked mining concessions cluster geographically within the Lualaba/Haut-Katanga copper-cobalt belt, or are they interleaved with non-Chinese operators?
verification_status: ✅ Confirmed (test rerun with sensitivity check; ownership sources listed per concession, ambiguous cases marked unknown rather than guessed)

data_source.geometry: OpenStreetMap Overpass API, landuse=quarry, live query of the Lualaba/Haut-Katanga bounding box
data_source.note: OSM tags individual pits, not concession boundaries. TFM alone (a single 1,600 sq km concession) is split across 23 separate OSM polygons (Tenke Pit, Kwatebala Mine, Mwadinkomba East/West Mine, Shimbidi Pit, and 18 others). All same-concession sub-pits were dissolved into one spatial unit before testing, to avoid counting one concession's internal pit subdivisions as if they were neighboring, independent mines.

ownership_attribution.method: Web research per named site: company annual reports/investor pages, Wikipedia, Mongabay, Global Witness, mindat.org, portergeo.com.au, the TFM 2014 NI 43-101 technical report, Reuters/Mining.com/Afrikarabia news coverage. Unresolved names are marked unknown rather than inferred from proximity alone.

china_linked.confidence: medium - sources conflict on scope with the adjacent Gecamines-operated smelter

joint_venture.operator: Ivanhoe Mines (Canada) 39.6% + Zijin Mining (China) 39.6% + DRC govt 20%

non_china.operator: Glencore (Switzerland), via Katanga Mining, formally shuttered
Eurasian Resources Group (Kazakhstan), via Boss Mining SARL
Gecamines (DRC state), formally closed 2004, extensive artisanal activity
Chemaf / Virtus Minerals (US), control transferred March 2026 after a blocked Chinese (Norinco) bid

different_commodity.reason: cement, not copper/cobalt - excluded from the belt test though ownership is documented

artisanal_no_corporate_owner.operator: CMDS artisanal cooperative on an inactive Gecamines concession

not_a_distinct_concession: G E C A M I N E S (facility label)

ownership_attribution.flagged_naming_collisions: Shamitumba and Ludjiba: geological references (mindat.org) place both near Shinkolobwe (Haut-Katanga), not near Tenke Fungurume (Lualaba), despite falling inside this dataset's search bounding box. Left unattributed rather than guessed.

test.method: libpysal (KNN spatial weights, k=3) + esda (Join_Counts, 999 permutations), run on the 15 confidently-attributed units only
test.interpretation: No detectable spatial clustering of Chinese-linked concessions relative to the broader mining landscape - if anything, observed same-type neighbor pairs run below the random-chance expectation in both codings. Each of the 7-8 China-linked units' nearest neighbors include at least one non-Chinese-linked operator (Glencore, ERG, Gecamines, or the US-controlled Etoile mine) - there is no geographically distinct 'Chinese zone' within the belt.
test.caveat: Only 15 of 145 mapped concessions in this belt have a confirmed operator in this dataset - low statistical power given the small labeled sample, and the test describes the well-documented majors, not the full mining landscape (111 of 171 raw OSM polygons carry no name at all).

reproducibility.note: Weights built on projected coordinates (EPSG:32735, UTM 35S) over the centroids of the 15 dissolved, confidently-labeled concession polygons.
